behaviors.description: The Linux audit daemon was stopped or disabled. Turning off the sensor that records what happens next is defense impairment in its plainest form — legitimate only inside a maintenance window. Distinct from history clearing (T1070.003): this disables future evidence rather than destroying past evidence.
false_positives: Planned maintenance windows and host reboots — corroborate against change records
behaviors.name: auditd_stopped
behaviors.title: Audit Daemon Stopped or Disabled

behaviors.description: certutil.exe fetching from a URL is living-off-the-land ingress tool transfer: a signed certificate utility repurposed as a downloader. The behavior (LOLBin + URL) outlives any particular payload host. Requires endpoint command-line telemetry.
false_positives: Legitimate certificate-store maintenance rarely touches URLs — verify the fetched origin
behaviors.name: certutil_remote_download
behaviors.title: Certutil Used to Fetch a Remote File

behaviors.description: Writing an @reboot cron entry — or dropping a file into /etc/cron.d — gives a payload execution that survives restarts. The persistence mechanism is the durable behavior; the payload path changes per intrusion. Requires command-line or file-write telemetry.
false_positives: Configuration-management tools (Ansible, Puppet) installing scheduled jobs — filter their runner accounts
behaviors.name: cron_reboot_persistence
behaviors.title: Cron Entry Installed for Reboot Persistence

behaviors.description: memfd_create followed by execution gives a payload that never touches disk — no file for hash matching to find, which is precisely why the syscall behavior itself is the indicator. Requires auditd syscall telemetry (memfd_create / execveat) that this platform does not yet ingest.
false_positives: Runtimes using memfd for legitimate JIT or sandboxing (some browsers, systemd-nspawn) — baseline per host role
behaviors.name: memfd_fileless_execution
behaviors.title: Fileless Execution via memfd_create

behaviors.description: A document-handling application (Word, Excel, Outlook) spawning a command interpreter is the classic malicious-document detonation: documents render content, they do not administer systems. Requires endpoint process telemetry (Sysmon EID 1 / auditd execve with parent linkage) that this platform does not yet ingest — the rule ships validated against synthetic fixtures and is labeled accordingly.
false_positives: Office add-ins that legitimately shell out (rare; inventory and filter them explicitly)
behaviors.name: office_app_spawns_shell
behaviors.title: Office Application Spawns a Command Shell

behaviors.description: A command line disabling real-time protection or stopping an endpoint security service. An administrator does this rarely and with a ticket; an intruder does it first. Requires endpoint command-line telemetry.
false_positives: Endpoint-agent upgrades performed by the management platform itself
behaviors.name: security_tool_tamper_command
behaviors.title: Endpoint Security Tooling Disabled from the Command Line

behaviors.description: Appending to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys from a shell grants credential-free access that survives password rotation — key-based persistence in one line. Requires command-line telemetry; file-integrity monitoring on authorized_keys is the complementary control.
false_positives: Legitimate key distribution by provisioning tooling — filter the deployment account
behaviors.name: ssh_authorized_keys_appended
behaviors.title: SSH Authorized Keys Appended from the Command Line
